scope: Independent candidate4 native memory-write audience contract review against candidate3; no claim of live recall or learning improvement

contractAssessment.behavior: Reject unsupported new audience before persistence
contractAssessment.evidence: Only user/agent/organization are advertised for writes. Raw scope=project or any projectId presence, including empty/null/undefined, throws before schema stripping, redaction or MemoryService.writeMemory. No alternate-scope write or retry was added.

contractAssessment.behavior: Protected execution does not silently strip the legacy projectId
contractAssessment.evidence: Existing validateToolArguments has removeAdditional=false, coerceTypes=false and useDefaults=false, and executeProtectedTool passes the unchanged input to tool.run after validation. Thus a legacy argument can fail at schema validation before the handler, while direct native invocation reaches its explicit fail-closed guard.

contractAssessment.behavior: New owner identity stays trusted and organization authority remains enforced
contractAssessment.evidence: resolveOwnerId uses canonical context user/org identity and current profile. Organization writes still require org admin or platform-admin authority. The handler never uses model-supplied owner IDs or project membership. Tests deny foreign user/profile/org mutation and retain supported cross-session lookup after SQLite reopen.

contractAssessment.behavior: Legacy session-owned project compatibility is preserved
contractAssessment.evidence: Read scope keeps project, resolves only context.sessionId, and fails when required session/principal is absent. Unscoped visibility still uses only organization/profile/user. Existing mutation checks retain org + matching owner, so the original session may update/delete its legacy rows while other tested sessions/organizations may not.

All2072 baseline source members were hash checked. Only the one production memory-tools.ts file and the existing dedup test differ; the only added source is the scope-contract test. DB/service/schema/migrations are unchanged. SQLite reopen verifies legacy owner/content/metadata preservation and no new access path for arbitrary-owner buckets.

baselineEvidence.interpretation: Both adapter rejection cases previously resolved rather than rejecting. Other compatibility cases passed. This is a behavior reproduction, not a model-performance experiment.

compatibilityAndScopeLimits: Intentional native API contraction: new project-scope writes are rejected, not automatically mapped or migrated. Existing callers using project/projectId must choose an authorized supported audience explicitly.
Legacy arbitrary-project-owner rows remain stored and receive no newly added repair/retrieval path; this patch does not solve durable shared-project membership.
Legacy session identity is not a newly established per-user privacy boundary. Trusted session authorization remains the outer caller responsibility, as before.
Direct lower-level MemoryService/database project operations remain unchanged for trusted callers.
Tests exercise real native tool handlers with trusted synthetic ToolContext plus in-memory and reopened SQLite adapters; no full AgentService/native account lifecycle or provider was run.
No production-wide or native-heavy suite was run while the paid candidate3 study was active. Root owns later integration and candidate freeze.
